judge_verdict.summary: The agent submitted a paper-derived scaling law that extrapolated poorly (test R²≈0.98, below the 0.995 gate) and declared success despite visible point-wise errors.

verdict.outcome_rationale: This was a genuine agent-fault failure and the verifier's FAIL is correct. The held-out harness scored the submission at R²=0.981869 on the hidden test split and then zeroed binary_reward because that score did not exceed the 0.995 pass threshold [1][2]. The task required discovering a vocabulary scaling law, writing `/app/law.py` and `/app/explain.md`, and extrapolating to unseen points on a hidden dataset [3], but instead of fitting the dataset's direct power-law form embodied in the reference solution [4], the agent ran web searches for external scaling-law literature [5], imported Tao et al.'s embedding-and-compression formulation, and built `law.py` to reload `/app/data` and re-optimize coefficients on every call [6]. At verification time `/app/data` was absent, triggering the hardcoded fallback path that produced the reported R² [7]. The agent's own checks before stopping showed a ~0.61 error on the first training point (true −1.349 vs predicted −0.740) and similar early-point residuals, yet it rationalized the mismatch as noise from aggregate MSE≈0.0097 and declared the task complete [8][9]. That insufficient self-validation left a model that never approached the required extrapolation quality on the hidden test set, so the task was not truly solved even though the deliverable files existed [1][10].
